function: DQN learns movable-antenna velocity actions (MA trajectory) at the BS; beamforming and RIS phase are optimized per slot by non-learned AO (SDR, penalty) for covert rate (pp. 5-9).
system: BS with M movable antennas (M = 2, 4, 8); single-antenna Bob and Willie; reflecting RIS, N = 12; carrier wavelength 0.108 m, frequency not stated (pp. 3, 9).
method: AO-based DQN: Q-network with two ReLU hidden layers of 128 units, discrete velocity actions, epsilon-greedy, replay buffer, target network; reinforcement learning; the inner AO is not learned (pp. 6-10).
data_channel: Simulated field-response MA channel to the RIS with Rayleigh small-scale fading, 4 paths, path-loss exponent 2.2; Rician RIS-Bob link; no 3GPP model or measurements (pp. 4, 10).
test_conditions: Not stated whether the DQN is retrained per setting: figures sweep power, region size, antennas, RIS elements, RIS-BS distance and spacing, each averaged over 1000 channel realizations (pp. 10-13).
baselines: Non-learned: AO with fixed-position antennas (FPA), AO with random MA trajectory; learned: AO with Dueling DQN, global DDPG controlling trajectory, beamforming and phase (p. 10).
metrics: Covert rate (bits/s/Hz) versus training episodes, AO iterations, transmit power, region size, number of antennas and RIS elements, RIS-BS distance, antenna spacing (pp. 10-13).
complexity: Order only for the non-learned AO: O(I_iter(I_o I_i(2N^3.5) + I_o I_i(2M^3.5))); none for the DQN (p. 9).
openness: none (no code or data link; only software versions: Python 3.10, PyTorch 1.6, Cvxpy 1.5.2, p. 10).
q1_support: p. 10: "small-scale channel fading component, modeled as Rayleigh fading". Custom field-response MA channel with Rayleigh and Rician fading and path-loss exponent 2.2 (pp. 4, 10); no 3GPP TR 38.901/38.811, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 10: "Each data point in the simulation results is obtained by averaging over 1000 independent channel realizations". Held-out channel realizations only; the paper never states that a trained DQN is tested with other antenna, RIS or region settings than in training (state size depends on M, p. 7).
q3_support: p. 10: "Global Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG): The movement of MA is governed by DDPG, while beamforming as well as phase is under the control of DDPG." Also p. 10: "AO-Based FPA: The BS is equipped with M uniform linear array antennas". The covert rate of the proposed method is compared with non-learned AO-FPA and random schemes and with Dueling DQN and DDPG (Figs. 8-12, pp. 11-13).
q4_support: p. 9: "the total complexity of the AO algorithm is" O(I_iter(I_o I_i(2N^3.5) + I_o I_i(2M^3.5))). Only the non-learned AO part of the AO-based DQN is covered; no cost (parameters, FLOPs, runtime) of the DQN is reported.
q5_support: p. 10: "The experimental environments for the DQN network and the AO algorithm are as follows: Python 3.10, PyTorch 1.6, and Cvxpy 1.5.2." Custom simulation (Table I, p. 10); no code or data link and no public channel dataset.
notes: Included as area 3 with a borderline function call: the only learned element is the DQN that outputs movable-antenna velocity actions (pp. 6-8), while beamforming and RIS phase come from the non-learned AO algorithm (pp. 8-9). MA positioning is read here as BS array configuration for beamforming in a RIS-aided link, not as antenna hardware design; if the reviewer rejects this reading, the code would be function. q3: Dueling DQN and DDPG are standard learners on the same problem, AO-FPA and random are non-learned (p. 10). q4 rests on the AO complexity only.
